tool_summary: Changes file owner and group. Transferring ownership to root or another user can affect who has effective control over a file, and -R applies the change across an entire directory tree at once.
platform_notes: Core syntax (owner[:group], -R, -h) is consistent between GNU and BSD chown.

rules.description: Recursively transferring ownership of a directory tree to root removes the invoking (typically non-root) user's ability to modify those files without elevated privileges, and can affect files the operator did not intend to include if the tree is large or contains unexpected symlinks.

Recursively applies an ownership change across an entire directory tree at once. This is worth attention independent of privilege level or target user: recursion is inherently harder to scope correctly (a mistaken path, an unexpected symlink, or a broader tree than intended can all be affected), and neither commandant nor chown itself records the prior owner to allow a clean undo. Combined with -L/-H (dereference symlinks), can also affect files outside the target directory if symlinks point elsewhere.
rules.reversible_note: Neither chown nor commandant records the prior owner of affected files, so a recursive change cannot be cleanly undone without separately-recorded state.
